what_it_measured.text: The effects on actin were then determined by measuring the amount of binding of fluorescent phalloidin with quantitative image analysis.

Fluorescence images were recorded with a Zeiss Axiovert 10 microscope (Zeiss) coupled to a cooled CCD camera (Star I; Photometrics, Tucson, AZ) using a 100-W quartz-halogen lamp and either a 25x/NA 0.8 Plan-Neofluar or a 10Ox/NA 1.3 Neofluar objective (Zeiss).

dose.text: For most of the experiments, thymosin peptides were dissolved in 5 mM Tris acetate (pH 6.95) containing 3 mg of fixable fluorescein-conjugated dextran (Molecular Probes) per ml at a concentration of 0.48-1.63 mM.

route.text: Pressure microinjection was performed as described (4, 30).

endpoint.text: At t=0, the solution was mixed with 0.5 volume of 3 x polymerization buffer (6 mM MgCl2/0.3 M KCI/3 mM ATP/75 mM imidazole, pH 7.0), and the fluorescence intensity was measured in a spectrofluorimeter (LS-3; Perkin-Elmer) at an excitation wavelength of 365 nm and an emission wavelength of 407 nm.
Actin polymerization was measured by the increase of fluorescence intensity of pyrene-labeled actin.

To quantify the effect of P4 on actin assembly, we measured the relative amount of actin filaments in NRK cells by integrating the total fluorescence intensity of bound rhodamine-phalloidin within the cellular boundary.

numbers.text: For most of the experiments, thymosin peptides were dissolved in 5 mM Tris acetate (pH 6.95) containing 3 mg of fixable fluorescein-conjugated dextran (Molecular Probes) per ml at a concentration of 0.48-1.63 mM.
Pressure microinjection was performed as described (4, 30).

At t=0, the solution was mixed with 0.5 volume of 3 x polymerization buffer (6 mM MgCl2/0.3 M KCI/3 mM ATP/75 mM imidazole, pH 7.0), and the fluorescence intensity was measured in a spectrofluorimeter (LS-3; Perkin-Elmer) at an excitation wavelength of 365 nm and an emission wavelength of 407 nm.

Fluorescence images were recorded with a Zeiss Axiovert 10 microscope (Zeiss) coupled to a cooled CCD camera (Star I; Photometrics, Tucson, AZ) using a 100-W quartz-halogen lamp and either a 25x/NA 0.8 Plan-Neofluar or a 10Ox/NA 1.3 Neofluar objective (Zeiss).
